title: Does Virgo's spot-tail Gray-Scott system give swimming, dividing spots with a losable heritable tail, and so set the reaction-diffusion bar that beyond-diffusion swim-and-divide claims must beat?
summary: Froese, Virgo & Ikegami (Artificial Life 2014; the system is from N. Virgo's 2011 thesis) describe a pure reaction-diffusion world with two autocatalysts. A Gray-Scott spot carries a tail of a second autocatalyst that feeds on it; together they swim away from the tail at about 4e-4 units per time unit, and they duplicate. Tails usually pass to the daughters ('limited heredity with variation'), and tailed spots win only where cataclysms clear space. C:swim-divide-bd and P_BD assume that plain reaction-diffusion cannot swim and divide, so this baseline should be reproduced once and its scores recorded as the bar.
